When will I use this?

Speed, distance and time: when will I use this?

Whenever you need to know how long, how far or how fast.

IT support technician

Digital

\(\displaystyle t = \dfrac{\text{size} \times 8}{\text{speed}}\)

How long will a 600 MB update take?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Broadband is sold in megabits per second (Mbit/s), but files are measured in megabytes (MB). 8 megabits = 1 megabyte. A 600 MB update on an 80 Mbit/s line (example figures):

  1. In megabits: \(600 \times 8 = 4800\).
  2. Time: \(4800 \div 80 = 60\) seconds.

The answer: \(600 \times 8 \div 80 = 60\) seconds

HGV driver

Transport and logistics

\(\displaystyle t = \dfrac{d}{s}\)

Does this run need a legal break?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Lorry drivers must take a 45-minute break after 4½ hours of driving. A 270-mile run at an average of 50 mph (example figures):

  1. Driving time: \(270 \div 50 = 5.4\) hours = 5 h 24 min \((0.4 \times 60 = 24)\).
  2. That's over 4½ hours, so a 45-minute break goes in: 5 h 24 min + 45 min = 6 h 09 min door to door.

The answer: \(270 \div 50 = 5.4\) hours

Roads policing officer

Protective services

\(\displaystyle s = \dfrac{d}{t}\)

Was this car speeding between the cameras?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Average speed cameras time a car between two cameras a known distance apart. The cameras are 3 miles apart; a car takes 3 min 20 s; the limit is 50 mph (example figures).

  1. Time: 3 min 20 s = 200 seconds = \(200 \div 3600 = 1/18\) of an hour.
  2. Speed: \(3 \times 18 = 54\) mph: over the limit.

The answer: \(3 \times 18 = 54\) mph

Practise it

Games on MaffsGames that practise speed, distance and time:

  • Formula Plug-In: Substitute values into formulae and work out the answer, from simple rules to area and speed.
  • Football Pitches per Squared Squirrel: Speed, density, pressure and unit price: read the unit and you know the calculation, because km/h means km ÷ h.

  • HGV driver: GOV.UK / DVSA, "Drivers' hours: HGV driver basics"
